ticket.title: Audit: only GB-71 was archived while still open, no other open ticket is archived
ticket.description: INFORMATIONAL, closed. Audit performed after GB-71 turned up archived while it was still an open Ready task: is anything else incorrectly archived? Evidence, taken from the from field every archive event records: 57 tasks remain archived and all 57 recorded from=verified, so they are completed work. Exactly one archive had from=ready - GB-71 - and it was restored before the work began. Cross-checking the open set against the archived set returns zero overlap: 29 open tickets, none archived. So the data is sound and the single incorrect archive was the one already noticed. The underlying cause was not the archive operation but its caller, which supplied whatever ids it happened to render; that is fixed in GB-177 by archiving server-side from a filter, so a client can no longer under-supply the set.

task.title: Audit: only GB-71 was archived while still open, no other open ticket is archived
task.description: The bulk archive pass archived 58 tasks and GB-71 was one of them while it was still a Ready backlog item, not completed work - which is how a P2 refactor disappeared from the board and then had to be unarchived when it was picked up. Audit of the current state with the ledger from field as evidence: 57 tasks remain archived and every one of them recorded from=verified, so GB-71 was the single incorrect archive and nothing else is lost. Cross-check confirms no currently open ticket is archived (29 open, zero overlap). The archive operation itself did not distinguish completed from open work because it archived whatever ids its caller supplied, which is the same defect GB-177 records - this ticket exists to keep the data finding separate from the caller-selection fix.
